base.role: BASE TEMPLATE / rig anchor — not an on-screen character; seeds the cast for form.

macgregor.role: Gregor MacGregor — the con-man 'Cazique of Poyais'; recurring lead antagonist.
macgregor.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: deep crimson hussar coat with gold frogging, gold fringed epaulettes, silver-ribboned gold order-star medal (his self-awarded-decorations identity tag), dark trousers, dark boots; swept dark-brown hair + mutton-chop sideburns. Every appearance renders in this unless the shot deliberately authors a change (e.g. prince regalia over it).

bolivar.role: Simón Bolívar — the South-American liberator general; MacGregor's celebrated comrade-in-arms (appears L18).
bolivar.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: dark navy-blue liberator general's military coat with gold epaulettes and gold trim, a single bright red ceremonial sash worn diagonally across the chest, a black liberator's bicorne hat worn corner-forward, dark trousers and boots; short dark curly hair with prominent dark sideburns. Every appearance renders in this unless the shot deliberately authors a change.

mosquito-king.role: The Miskito Coast king who granted MacGregor the Poyais land in 1820 (appears L19–L20).
mosquito-king.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: a tall gold crown and a full-length ornate red-and-gold patterned ceremonial robe with British-influenced regalia (gold braiding, epaulettes, a red-and-gold patterned mantle over the shoulders); short dark hair. Every appearance renders in this unless the shot deliberately authors a change.

strangeways.role: Captain Thomas Strangeways — the fictitious 'author' of the Poyais guidebook (invented by MacGregor to sell the con); a bookish naval author-captain. Appears L35/L43/L44.
strangeways.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: plain dark navy double-breasted captain coat with a high collar and two rows of small brass buttons, thin round wire spectacles, short neat dark-brown hair combed down over the sides, dark trousers and boots. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

hastie.role: James Hastie — a weary Scottish sawyer and a leader of the Poyais settler survivors; signs the sworn statement exposing the fraud. Appears L104/L106.
hastie.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: worn brown working-man coat over a tan waistcoat and dark neckcloth, tousled greying-brown hair, sturdy build, plain trousers and boots. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

hastie-wife.role: The wife of James Hastie — a Poyais settler survivor at his side; quiet grief on the grey British quay. Appears L104.
hastie-wife.costume: PINNED canonical outfit (human-picked cand-1, 2026-07-16): long muted-earth wool dress, dark shawl, apron, worn boots, cream linen mob cap, front-facing neutral. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

miniscribe-rep.role: MiniScribe personified — the disk-drive company as an actor; the bricks story's lead. Appears L26-L35, L39, L40.
miniscribe-rep.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: boxy tan blazer worn open over a brown open-collar shirt (chest and lapels plain — no badge, pin, or logo), plain dark trousers and dark shoes; short dark-brown side-parted hair, stocky build. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

ibm-suit.role: IBM personified — the customer institution as an actor; MiniScribe's PC/XT contract buyer. Appears L30, L39.
ibm-suit.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: crisp navy pinstripe three-piece suit (jacket, matching waistcoat, trousers) over a white shirt with a plain dark tie, ONE plain white pocket square folded at the breast pocket (its single identity tag), polished dark shoes; close-cropped grey hair, broad heavy mass on the squat base proportion. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

rifenburgh-ceo.role: Richard Rifenburgh — the post-collapse MiniScribe CEO who fronts the press arc. Appears L177, L185.
rifenburgh-ceo.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: plain unpatterned charcoal TWO-piece suit (no waistcoat) over a white shirt with a plain muted-blue tie, dark shoes; short side-parted dark-brown hair (the cast's only dark-haired executive). Carries NO badge, pin, logo, pocket square, tie clip, watch chain or jewellery. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

terry-johnson.role: Terry Johnson — MiniScribe's founder; depicted at work and at his late-1984 departure. Appears L28, L42.
terry-johnson.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: white business shirt in shirtsleeves with both cuffs turned back to the forearm, a thin dark tie, plain dark trousers and dark shoes, no jacket; thinning fair hair combed back with the side hair filling the ear gap, one small trimmed fair moustache, lean build. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

pc-boxy.role: Personified beige boxy 1980s home computer — a FACED machine character (not a human). The cast's cartoon eyes and mouth sit in its front panel; short stubby arms and legs, NO hands. Appears L01-L04, L16.
pc-boxy.costume: PINNED canonical form: beige boxy home-computer case with the cast's cartoon eyes and mouth set into the front panel, short stubby arms and legs. NOTE: a personified OBJECT — never seed a human torso POSE frame onto it (bleeds a human body); expression frames route to the face panel and stance is carried in words.

auditor-rep.role: The outside AUDITOR personified — the accounting firm's man sent to verify MiniScribe's inventory; the figure the brick-filled cartons were staged for. Appears L141-L143, L145, L147, L166, L201, L202, L213, L242.
auditor-rep.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: dark charcoal three-piece suit (jacket, matching waistcoat, trousers) over a white shirt with a plain charcoal tie, ONE pair of round spectacles pushed up onto the forehead (its single identity tag), dark shoes; short dark-brown hair, clean-shaven. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

brick-foreman.role: The MiniScribe warehouse/division man — rank-and-file management: packs the bricks, takes the envelope, carries the fraud's human middle. Currently UNCAST: the 2026-08-06 shots.json re-author dropped his 30 shots (L60-L201 in the prior authoring); the canonical is retained for re-cast.
brick-foreman.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: cream short-sleeve button shirt with a narrow dark charcoal clip-on tie and tie bar, mid-brown trousers, brown shoes; short mid-brown side-parted hair, clean-shaven, plain build. No jacket, no badge. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

hq-banker.role: The lending BANK personified — the institution whose money the inflated numbers were raised against. Appears L49-L51, L205, L206, L213.
hq-banker.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: brown chalk-stripe three-piece suit (jacket, matching waistcoat, trousers) over a white shirt with a brown tie, ONE gold watch chain swagged across the waistcoat (its single identity tag), brown shoes; swept silver-grey hair, clean-shaven, heavy build. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

line-worker.role: An anonymous MiniScribe assembly-line worker — the human cost of the fraud, not a lead. Minted 2026-08-12 in the G4 slice for L46's human-cost beat. Appears L46.
line-worker.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: knee-length grey cotton work coat worn open over an olive button shirt and dark charcoal trousers, sleeves pushed to the forearm, plain dark work shoes; short black side-parted hair, clean-shaven, plain build. No badge, no tie. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

qt-wiles.role: Q.T. Wiles — MiniScribe's chairman, the pressure at the top of the fraud. A BUSINESSMAN, never a physician: 'Dr. Fix-It' is a nickname only (Daniel's ruling, 2026-07-30), so no stethoscope, white coat, scrubs or medical prop in any shot, ever. Appears in 29 shots, L54-L236.
qt-wiles.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: steel-grey three-piece suit (jacket, matching waistcoat, trousers) over a white shirt with a grey tie, ONE gold tie clip (its single identity tag), brown shoes; swept silver-grey hair, clean-shaven, lean build. No spectacles, no pocket square. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

drive-maker.role: The hard-drive TRADE personified — the industry as an actor, carrying the picks-and-shovels beats before MiniScribe is disclosed (L18-L21), and, on a boss-accepted ruling, doubling as the rival buyer Maxtor at L233/L234 ~200 shots later. PLANNED at VPW step 3a 2026-08-13, not yet minted. Appears L18-L21, L233, L234.
drive-maker.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: brown knee-length warehouse coat worn open over a plain collarless shirt, a flat cap, mid-brown trousers and work boots; short sandy hair, wiry build. The breast pocket is left plain and the collar open. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

bond-investor.role: The MiniScribe BONDHOLDER personified — the retail investor who bought on the fake numbers, sues, wins the headline verdict, watches it evaporate and collects a quarter. Carries the final act's human cost. PLANNED at VPW step 3a 2026-08-13, not yet minted. Appears L194, L195, L197, L199, L209, L210, L212, L237.
bond-investor.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: fawn knitted cardigan over an open-collar shirt, brown corduroy trousers, tartan slippers; thin grey hair combed over, wire-rimmed spectacles, slight build. The slippers are load-bearing — later beats play on him never having changed out of them. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

return-customer.role: The COMPLICIT CUSTOMER personified — the distributor who agreed in advance to leave the pallets shrink-wrapped and mail them back, so the same bricks counted twice. PLANNED at VPW step 3a 2026-08-13, not yet minted. Appears L132, L133, L134, L136.
return-customer.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: navy quilted delivery coat with the breast patch left plain and unlettered, dark trousers, heavy boots, a knitted navy beanie pushed back; dark beard, broad build. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

brick-co-seller.role: The Colorado Brick Company personified — sells the 26,000 bricks and is the story's last laugh, the one party that came out ahead. PLANNED at VPW step 3a 2026-08-13, not yet minted (was named-but-unminted in the 2026-08-06 file). Appears L115, L239, L240.
brick-co-seller.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: dusty tan work shirt with the sleeves rolled, a heavy canvas apron, a wide-brimmed straw hat worn square, dark work trousers and boots; weathered face, greying moustache. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change (L239 deliberately pushes the hat back).

tv-chef.role: A GENERIC television kitchen-rescue host — the archetype the script's Gordon Ramsay aside invokes, staged so Wiles can occupy the identical frame one cut later. NEVER a likeness of the real named cook (imagery policy: no depiction of a real named person). PLANNED at VPW step 3a 2026-08-13, not yet minted. Appears L55, L56, L60.
tv-chef.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: double-breasted white chef's jacket with the sleeves shoved to the elbow, a mid-blue apron tied at the waist, dark checked trousers; cropped fair hair, heavy build, bare-headed. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

trial-judge.role: The trial JUDGE — throws the $550M verdict out days after the jury returned it, the video's biggest reversal. PLANNED at VPW step 3a 2026-08-13, not yet minted. Appears L207, L208.
trial-judge.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: black judicial robe over a white wing collar, full-rim reading spectacles low on the nose; close-cropped white hair, jowly build. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.

hr-officer.role: HR personified — the one force that actually beat the fraud, and the withheld peak's punchline. The cast's only woman. PLANNED at VPW step 3a 2026-08-13, not yet minted. Appears L243.
hr-officer.costume: PINNED canonical outfit: rust-red knitted cardigan over a cream blouse, a long tweed skirt, flat shoes; dark hair pinned up, reading spectacles on a chain, slight build. Renders in this unless a shot authors a change.
